164128.overview:
This is a remake of a Bally-Midway arcade game. You control a spaceship and shoot down the enemy "Droid" ships that attack you. Your ship must survive Droid-dropped mines too--but you can shoot them too. The last ship of the Droid flights goes into a spiraling pattern.

There is no end to this game. Rather, it is a game in which you try to get the highest score, or complete the highest number of levels.

You control a small triangle that is your ship. The ship can turn, move forward (with thrusters) and fire. Movement is one of the games challenges; once the ship is moving, it can only be slowed by turning the nose in the opposite direction and use the thrusters. While doing that, the ship is unable to fire toward anything it is in motion toward.

Bouncing also comes into play during movement. When the ship hits the side of the screen, a wall of force appears, and the ship bounces. You don't have control over where the ship bounces, and must take time to regain control, before you run into an enemy ship and die.

164251.overview: Protect the VICs by shooting meteors that line up like the Space Invaders before falling down one by one.

164960.overview: The play mechanic is a mix of many games; protecting your ground-based city with a moving crosshair is obviously Missile Command.  However, the asteroids that drop on you break into two and then four pieces as in Asteroids.  And the force field over a cityscape looks a lot like Imagic's Atlantis game.

176194.overview:
Operation Ganymed is a 1-player arcade game for the VIC-20.

Your lunar module is low on fuel and your mission is to unload badly needed supplies to a remote colony. The three landing sites lie among the caverns and cliffs of the Altai Mountains. Your mission is complete when all three sites have received supplies. With only three modules at your disposal, you must land accurately on each site at exactly the right rate of descent. Too fast or out of position and you will blow up on impact. Points are given for the amount of fuel and for low landing speeds. The player's spaceship is refilled with each successful landing. After landing on all 3 sites, gravity is increased.

Developed and initially published in 1994 by Atlantis Software in Europe, it was later released the same year in North America by Laing Marketing.

454445.overview:
The 'O' Level Caper is a 1-player arcade and text adventure combination for the VIC-20.

Contains two separate games spread over 2 cassettes with a text adventure and arcade component.

In the arcade component, the player controls a character who moves laterally, jumps, and climbs ladders between platforms. The player must avoid or jump over barrels thrown from above that roll along platforms and down ladders. The goal is to collect all items present on the platform while avoiding dangers. The player has 3 lives, and proceeds to a more difficult level when all items are collected. After completing the first level, the player receives a pass code needed to play the text adventure.

In the text adventure component, the player tries to invade the local university. Multiple rooms of the university offer puzzles for the player to solve. The player can pick up and use items, and has limited inventory. All commands are via VERB NOUN entry. There is no save/restore feature.
